Any unauthenticated visitor can discover the installed pyyaml version (5.1), which is known to be vulnerable to deserialization attacks via yaml.load(). This version disclosure aids attackers in selecting appropriate exploit payloads. SOURCE: unauthenticated GET -> SINK: version string rendered in response.

extra.message: Observable Response Discrepancy in a1_broken_access_lab_1 — 'User Not Found' reveals valid credentials

metadata.proof: When POST credentials do not match jack:jacktheripper, the response returns 'User Not Found'. When they match, the response includes profile data. The distinct 'User Not Found' string allows an attacker to enumerate the single valid credential pair. SOURCE: POST body (name,pass) -> SINK: response body differs (User Not Found vs profile content).

extra.message: Observable Response Discrepancy in a1_broken_access_lab_2 — 'User Not Found' reveals valid credentials

metadata.proof: Same pattern as lab_1: the POST handler returns 'User Not Found' for invalid credentials vs profile content for valid jack:jacktheripper combo. The distinct 'User Not Found' string allows enumerating valid credentials. SOURCE: POST body (name,pass) -> SINK: response body differs (User Not Found vs profile content).

extra.message: No rate limiting on auth_lab_login POST endpoint

metadata.proof: The auth_lab_login POST handler at line 314 performs credential checking via authLogin.objects.filter(username=user_name,password=passwd)[0] with no rate limiting, account lockout, or incremental delay. An attacker can brute-force credentials against the authLogin model at full request speed. The GET handler at line 301 also allows user enumeration by trying sequential auto-increment userid cookie values. SOURCE: POST body (username,pass) -> SINK: database query executed with no throttle.

SOURCE: POST body (username,password) -> SINK: hardcoded comparison with no throttle.

extra.message: A7_disscussion_api has no authentication check

metadata.proof: The A7_disscussion_api at line 94 is decorated with @csrf_exempt and has NO authentication check (no @authentication_decorator, no request.user.is_authenticated). Any unauthenticated remote user can POST arbitrary code strings and receive differentiated responses (success/failure) based on whether the code contains the session-deletion pattern. This leaks information about the lab's expected solution without any access control. SOURCE: unauthenticated POST body -> SINK: code checked against search patterns.

extra.message: A6_disscussion_api has no authentication check

metadata.proof: The A6_disscussion_api at line 113 is decorated with @csrf_exempt and has NO authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can call this endpoint unlimited times. The check_vuln() call (imported from introduction.playground.A6.utility) performs dependency vulnerability scanning — an unauthenticated attacker can consume server CPU/network resources by flooding this endpoint, as there is no rate limiting or auth gate. SOURCE: unauthenticated request -> SINK: check_vuln() executed on server.

extra.message: Unlimited Docker container creation with no per-user quota

metadata.proof: The DoItFast.post method at line 45 spawns Docker containers via subprocess with no per-user limit on concurrent or total containers. The only constraint is the port range 8000-8100 (100 ports). An authenticated attacker can exhaust all 100 ports, then any legitimate user gets 'failed'. Additionally, each docker run consumes system memory/CPU. There is no cleanup of orphaned containers, no max_containers_per_user, and no rate limit on the POST handler. SOURCE: authenticated POST with challenge name -> SINK: docker run subprocess.

extra.message: Missing authorization: any authenticated user can spawn Docker containers

metadata.proof: SOURCE: authenticated user-controlled challenge name in URL -> DoItFast.post() looks up the Challenge and immediately executes subprocess.Popen() with docker run. No is_staff, role, or tenant check is enforced — the only gate is request.user.is_authenticated. Any logged-in user (including regular users) can launch arbitrary lab containers, consume host resources, and potentially reach other containers on the host network. SOURCE: authenticated user request -> SINK: docker run subprocess with no authorization check beyond authentication.

extra.message: User enumeration via password-reset response

metadata.proof: SOURCE: attacker-supplied email in /reset-password POST. If the email exists in the users dict, the endpoint flashes a password-reset link; if not found, it flashes 'Email not found' at line 92. These distinguishable responses reveal whether an account with that email is registered.

extra.message: User enumeration via registration response

metadata.proof: SOURCE: attacker-supplied username in /register POST. If the username already exists in the users dict, register() falls through to flash 'Registration failed' at line 78; if the username is new, it flashes 'Registration successful'. This success/failure discrepancy lets an attacker enumerate registered usernames.

extra.message: User enumeration via auth_lab_signup

metadata.proof: SOURCE: attacker-chosen username in auth_lab_signup POST. The authLogin model has username=unique=True, so creating a duplicate triggers an IntegrityError caught by the bare except block at line 297, which returns 'Username already exists'. If the username is new, the record is created and the success page is rendered. This reveals whether a username is already taken.

extra.message: Unrestricted file upload in a9_lab

metadata.proof: a9_lab accepts any uploaded file at line 558 and passes it directly to yaml.load() at line 560. There is no extension whitelist, MIME-type validation, magic-byte check, or size limit, allowing unauthenticated (or any authenticated) clients to upload and process arbitrary file types.

extra.message: Denial of service via unbounded image upload in a9_lab2

metadata.proof: a9_lab2 reads the uploaded file at line 582 into Image.open(), converts it, splits channels, runs ImageMath.eval(), and base64-encodes the result. No maximum file size is enforced, so a large or decompression-bomb image can exhaust worker memory and CPU.

extra.message: Denial of service via unbounded SSRF fetch in ssrf_lab2

metadata.proof: SOURCE: user-controlled URL POST parameter at line 960. ssrf_lab2 calls requests.get(url) at line 963 with no timeout, maximum response size, or streaming. A slow or giant response from an attacker-held endpoint can hang the Django worker or exhaust memory.

extra.message: Missing rate limiting on auth_lab_signup

metadata.proof: auth_lab_signup at line 279 creates authLogin rows from POST data without any rate limiting or throttling. Attackers can automate account creation, causing database bloat and enabling further brute-force or enumeration attacks.

extra.message: Session token stored in plaintext

metadata.proof: AF_session_id.session_id at line 84 stores the bearer token verbatim in the database. At views.py line ~1198-1200, AF_session_id.objects.create(session_id=token, ...) writes the raw token. A database compromise leaks active session tokens, and there is no server-side hashing or revocation mechanism.
